trends.source: Google Trends. United States, past 12 months, average search interest (0-100 index, a two-term comparison of "weed" against "dispensary"). Cited from Google Trends, NOT computed from this book’s scan data.
trends.note: weed draws roughly twice the search interest of dispensary, the agency optimized the smaller term.

sec.argument: The agency optimized the smaller term. On "dispensary near me", worth about half the search interest of "weed near me" by Google Trends, only 139 of 280 storefronts (49.6%) are one of the three businesses Google shows most often around their own address; the other 141 sit #4 or worse, or never make the top three from a single spot searched. On "weed near me", worth roughly twice as much, and the word customers actually type, 275 of 280 (98.2%) are invisible and only 5 rank. Same 280 storefronts, same store listings, opposite result by phrase: the "weed near me" invisibility is the phrase, not a data or listing error, and even the term they chose to chase leaves most of the book out of the pack.

onpage.population_definition: TWO LAYERS, and every published number reduces to the first one by a single visible step. MEASURED CORE (the *_sites, *_pages and *_images keys in this block): the 96 Screaming-Frog-attributable readable crawls, which is the active 99 minus the non-RRH rebuild (livefino.com) minus the 2 bot-walled 403 scanned failures (shop.starbuds.us, thrivedispensaries.com), whose single refused page is never counted as a MEASURED defect. Every measured SITE figure therefore caps at 96. PUBLISHED VIEW (published_99, below): the owner ruling of 2026-08-24 is that 99 is the base and a site that could not be scanned failed everything. So the denominator for anything that goes on the page is 99, and the 2 bot-walled sites are SCORED as failing every crawl-derived check. A published FAULT count is therefore the measured count plus 2; a published VIRTUE count is the measured count unchanged, because blocking a crawler does not give a site a title, a description, an H1 or a labelled image. PAGE and IMAGE counts do not move at all: the two refused sites served one error page each, and an error page is not a menu page and carries no images. The +2 is a SCORING RULING, not a measurement, and it is labelled as one everywhere it is applied. Cite the measured core for provenance; cite published_99 on the page.

published_99.ruling_quote: 99 is the base... if it can't be scanned it failed everything.
published_99.rule: Denominator 99 for every published figure. The 2 bot-walled sites (shop.starbuds.us, thrivedispensaries.com) blocked the crawler, and that is scored as failing every crawl-derived check, so a FAULT count publishes as measured + 2. A VIRTUE count publishes as measured, unchanged, because refusing a crawler does not give a site a title, a description, an H1 or a labelled image; only its denominator moves to 99. PAGE and IMAGE counts do not move at all.
published_99.is_a_ruling_not_a_measurement: The +2 is a SCORING DECISION taken by the publisher, not something the crawler observed. The crawler observed a 403 and nothing else. Every published fault figure here therefore carries its measured twin and its derivation, so any reader can subtract the ruling back out and see exactly what was measured.
published_99.carve_out_a_non_rrh: livefino.com is NOT covered by the ruling. Its crawl succeeded (crawl 168, 66 pages), so "it could not be scanned" does not apply to it. It is kept out of the fault numerators for a different reason: its current website is somebody else's rebuild, which is the one claim the agency could actually rebut. It STAYS INSIDE the 99 denominator and is simply not counted as failing. That is conservative in the agency's favour, and it is stated here rather than hidden. It is also why a published fault count plus its published virtue twin comes to 98 and not 99: the one site in neither column is livefino.com.
published_99.carve_out_b_measured_pass: "Failed everything" cannot override a MEASURED PASS. The fail-everything rule applies to the CRAWL-DERIVED checks that were actually blocked. PageSpeed Insights and the accessibility audit both ran on the 2 bot-walled sites and returned real numbers (shop.starbuds.us: PageSpeed 4, accessibility 73; thrivedispensaries.com: PageSpeed 12, accessibility 92). Where a check ran and returned a number, THE REAL NUMBER STANDS, and it is the number carried in this file. Marking a site as failing a check we measured it passing would be fabrication, and it is the one thing in this document that would hand the agency a way to discredit the rest. This carve-out is a stated assumption, not a measurement, and it belongs in the honesty box in these terms.

image_label_disclosure.check_that_did_run: the Google accessibility audit item "image-alt", read on the homepage only
image_label_disclosure.statement: The image-label figure is the one place where the ruling and a reading this file actually took point opposite ways on these 2 sites, so it is stated rather than left to be found. The sitewide check, whether every image carries a text label, reads every image on every page the crawler reaches; on these two it reached nothing, so the check never ran and the rule scores them as failing it, which is what takes the figure from 81 measured to 83 published. Google's accessibility audit does contain an image-label check, it did reach both homepages, and neither homepage failed it (shop.starbuds.us failed 2 other checks: the page does not say what language it is in (html-has-lang), no marked main content area (landmark-one-main); thrivedispensaries.com failed 3 other checks: an unnamed pop-up (aria-dialog-name), text too faint to read comfortably (color-contrast), buttons whose spoken name does not match their label (label-content-name-mismatch)). So the +2 on this particular check rests on the stated rule and not on any reading of an image. The two results are not in conflict: one audit reads one page, the sitewide check reads every page, and a homepage carrying labelled images is not evidence that the rest of a site does.

published_99.honesty_box: Two things in these numbers are decisions rather than measurements, and both are stated here. First, 2 of the 99 sites (shop.starbuds.us and thrivedispensaries.com) blocked the crawler outright. They are scored as failing every check the crawler was blocked from running, and they are counted in the 99. Second, that scoring does not extend to checks that actually ran. PageSpeed Insights and Google's accessibility audit both reached those two sites and came back with real numbers: shop.starbuds.us scored 4 on PageSpeed and 73 on accessibility, and thrivedispensaries.com scored 12 on PageSpeed and 92 on accessibility. Those are the numbers printed on this page. Where a check returned a number, the number stands, and marking a site down on a check it was seen to answer would be inventing evidence. Separately, livefino.com sits inside the 99 but is counted as failing nothing, because its current website is a rebuild the agency did not do. That choice is in the agency's favour and is why the failing and clean columns add up to 98 rather than 99. The image-label figure is the one place where the ruling and a reading this file actually took point opposite ways on these 2 sites, so it is stated rather than left to be found. The sitewide check, whether every image carries a text label, reads every image on every page the crawler reaches; on these two it reached nothing, so the check never ran and the rule scores them as failing it, which is what takes the figure from 81 measured to 83 published. Google's accessibility audit does contain an image-label check, it did reach both homepages, and neither homepage failed it (shop.starbuds.us failed 2 other checks: the page does not say what language it is in (html-has-lang), no marked main content area (landmark-one-main); thrivedispensaries.com failed 3 other checks: an unnamed pop-up (aria-dialog-name), text too faint to read comfortably (color-contrast), buttons whose spoken name does not match their label (label-content-name-mismatch)). So the +2 on this particular check rests on the stated rule and not on any reading of an image. The two results are not in conflict: one audit reads one page, the sitewide check reads every page, and a homepage carrying labelled images is not evidence that the rest of a site does.

published_99.how_to_quote: Fault line: use checks.<check>.fault.statement, for example "97 of 99". Virtue line: use checks.<check>.virtue.statement, for example "1 of 99". Page and image lines: quote pages_and_images_unchanged as-is and never attach the 99 site base to them. Never add 2 to a virtue, a page count or an image count. ONE CAUTION ON VIRTUE LINES: a virtue is measured over the 96 and stated of 99, and exactly one site (livefino.com) sits in neither the failing column nor the clean column, so a virtue line can understate the clean side by at most 1. sf_technical.zero_products_note: 55 sites returned zero crawlable product pages, and the 55 splits three ways. 52 are a direct MEASUREMENT of the menu plugin: the crawler read the menu and reached no product page. 2 (shop.starbuds.us, thrivedispensaries.com) refused the crawler with a 403, so their zero is an artifact of the refusal rather than a reading of a menu. 1 (livefino.com) is a non-RRH rebuild. TWO DIFFERENT SENTENCES COME OUT OF THIS BLOCK AND THEY MUST NEVER BE MERGED. (1) THE FAULT COUNT, which is what goes on the page of 99: under the owner ruling of 2026-08-24 a site that blocked the crawler is scored as failing every crawl-derived check, so the published fault is 54 of 99 (see zero_products_published_99). (2) THE MECHANISM CLAIM, that the product cards are drawn in by JavaScript inside boxes that are not links: that is an observation of a menu, it can only be made where a menu was actually read, and it is made on the 52 measured sites out of the 96 whose menus could be inspected. Never state the mechanism on 55, and never state the fault count on 52 of 99.

zero_products_published_99.mechanism_rule: The FAULT COUNT and the MECHANISM CLAIM are two different sentences and they carry two different numbers. The fault count is 54 of 99 and it says how many client sites return no product a link-following search engine can reach. The mechanism claim says WHY, that the product cards are drawn in by JavaScript inside boxes that are not links, and that is an observation of a menu, so it is only ever made on the 52 sites out of the 96 whose menus could actually be inspected. Never write the mechanism against 99 and never write the fault count against 52.

product_reach.sites_definition: The client sites whose newest crawl returned at least one crawlable product detail page. It is the complement of the 55 zero-product crawls inside the 99, and it is derived from the same flag: zero_products === false.
product_reach.page_definition: PRODUCT DETAIL PAGE: an HTML page of the newest crawl (any HTTP status) whose URL path is /products/<slug> or deeper, excluding the bare /products/ index page and the /products/page/N pagination URLs. This is the rule that produces the 55/44 split, so the count and the population share one definition. It is NOT the menu classifier rule behind menu_cluster.classifier_product_pages_total: that one matches the substring "/products/" at any depth and therefore also counts store-scoped catalog URLs, the bare index and pagination, which is why it totals more pages. Never quote one against the other.
